title: Air Ticket Fare Brands: Basis for Charging Voluntary Itinerary Changes
content:
A voluntary change to a ticket held under Air Ticket Fare Brands is priced as the change fee of the fare brand held plus, where the new itinerary costs more, the difference to the new fare. The amount raised on the change fee line is the change fee of the fare brand held.

**Changes carrying no fee.** A voluntary change is handled with no change fee only when frozen time is not after the moment the traveller's ticket was issued for this booking plus the free-change window of the fare brand held. The free-change window is counted in whole elapsed hours from the ticket issue moment, never mixing elapsed hours with calendar days, and a change made exactly at the boundary is still inside the window. The issue moment is taken from the record of the booking being changed, before the change is priced; the traveller's recollection of when the ticket issued is not the basis.

*On hypothetical figures:* a ticket issued at 09:00 on 3 September 2026, under a brand carrying a hypothetical free-change window of 36 whole elapsed hours, reaches the boundary at 21:00 on 4 September 2026. A change made at 21:00 that day is exactly at the boundary and inside the window, so no change fee arises; one made at 21:30 that day is after it, and the change fee of the fare brand held is raised.

**When a fee line may be raised.** A change fee line is raised only while the booking record stands at ticketed, read from the record of the booking the line would be raised against, before it is raised.

**Same-day moves.** A move between flights on the already-booked routing departing on the same calendar day is priced at the brand's same-day fee instead of the full change fee.

**Changes a brand does not allow.** A change that alters the origin or the destination is refused outright on a brand that does not allow routing changes, and a change of travel dates is refused outright on a brand that does not allow date changes. A refusal raises no fee line at all.

**The ceiling on changes.** The brand's ceiling on voluntary changes counts the traveller's voluntary changes on this ticket over the last twelve months. Once the ceiling is reached, a further change is refused and the traveller is offered cancellation on the brand's own terms instead.

**A cheaper new fare.** Where the new fare is cheaper than the fare already paid, the unused value is handled as the brand prescribes, whether forfeited, placed on a travel credit or returned to the original form of payment, and is never handled two ways at once.

**Airline schedule moves.** A change made necessary by an airline schedule move large enough to give the traveller a change right is not a voluntary change and carries no fee under this rule.
